body:
The crash was caused by us `abort()`ing in `ui_puts`:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/158f8b7ce3051127918148f7f8e9892a4c9ae34f/src/nvim/ui.c#L418-L420

Not sure what we were trying to "put", though.

Thanks for the report. Can you try the development version? 

The [Releases](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases) page has pre-built archives for Linux/Windows/macOS. (No installation needed, just unzip and run. For Linux, [nvim.appimage](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/nightly/nvim.appimage) is a universal "binary", just `chmod u+x nvim.appimage && ./nvim.appimage`)

Perhaps I wasn't clear; I am not quite able to replicate it (not great for debugging on your end), but I thought surely something that you would want to take a look at given it's a seg fault.

I just tried again in my installed version of nvim and was unable to replicate the issue. I tried quite hard too, as well :disappointed:

I managed to reproduce it: at the yesno prompt type some ctrl char, like `<C-E>`. (if you didn't type it, it could've come from a mapping or something). `message.c` needs to check the char is printable before sending it to `screen.c` .

@bfredl is right! all you need to do is as follows:

#### session 1
```
nvim<cr>
:e $MYVIMRC<cr>
```

#### session 2
```
nvim<cr>
:e $MYVIMRC<cr>
Go" random comment<esc>
:w<cr>
```

#### session 1 (again)

```
:w<cr>
<c-e>
```

then, you get a seg fault.

Now that I think about it, I believe I did accidentally hit something like `<c-e>` (as I was trying to scroll a little) just after the yes-no prompt popped up.

aside: I extracted the zip for the dev version for linux, and the same issue occurred in the dev version.

Cheers,
dylnmc
